{{one source|date=June 2020}}

In [[functional analysis]] and related areas of [[mathematics]], a '''quasi-ultrabarrelled space''' is a [[topological vector spaces]] (TVS) for which every [[Barrelled set|bornivorous ultrabarrel]] is a [[neighbourhood (topology)|neighbourhood]] of the origin. 

== Definition ==

A subset ''B''<sub>0</sub> of a TVS ''X'' is called a '''bornivorous ultrabarrel ''' if it is a closed, [[balanced set|balanced]], and [[Bornivorous set|bornivorous]] subset of ''X'' and if there exists a sequence <math>\left( B_{i} \right)_{i=1}^{\infty}</math> of closed balanced and bornivorous subsets of ''X'' such that ''B''<sub>''i''+1</sub> + ''B''<sub>''i''+1</sub> &sube; ''B''<sub>''i''</sub> for all ''i'' = 0, 1, .... 
In this case, <math>\left( B_{i} \right)_{i=1}^{\infty}</math> is called a '''defining sequence''' for ''B''<sub>0</sub>. 
A TVS ''X'' is called '''quasi-ultrabarrelled''' if every bornivorous ultrabarrel in ''X'' is a [[neighbourhood (topology)|neighbourhood]] of the origin.{{sfn | Khaleelulla | 1982 | pp=65-76}} 

== Properties ==

A [[locally convex]] quasi-ultrabarrelled space is [[Quasibarrelled space|quasi-barrelled]].{{sfn | Khaleelulla | 1982 | pp=65-76}} 

== Examples and sufficient conditions ==

[[Ultrabarrelled space]]s and [[ultrabornological space]]s are quasi-ultrabarrelled. 
Complete and metrizable TVSs are quasi-ultrabarrelled.{{sfn | Khaleelulla | 1982 | pp=65-76}}
